findings.element: .card[aria-expanded] / .card[data-open] — src/tasks.js:52 declares `let openNoteId = null; /* the card showing its full note */`, read at src/tasks.js:428 (draggable), :430 (aria-expanded), :434 (data-open) and :2828 (Escape → "Note closed."); consumed by src/tasks.css:954, :956, :957, :1179, :1976
findings.problem: openNoteId is never assigned anything but null. Every one of the fourteen assignments in tasks.js (542, 554, 661, 2829, 2899, 3098, 3319, 3476, 3632, 4185, 4367) sets it to null; nothing sets it to a task id. Measured consequences: every card with a note ships a permanent `aria-expanded="false"`, `draggable` is permanently "true", `data-open` is never emitted, so five CSS rules can never match — including tasks.css:954 `.card[data-open] .cardNote { max-height: none }`, the rule that was supposed to release the five-line note clamp, and tasks.css:1179's open ring. The Escape branch at 2828-2832 (`say("Note closed.")`) is unreachable, so that sentence is in the build and can never be spoken. Driving it confirms the mechanism moved: a real mouse-down/up on `.cardTitle` opens `.taskPanel`, moves focus into it and announces "Task open." — the in-place disclosure the comment on line 52 describes does not exist. Separately, CDP Accessibility.getPartialAXTree on the card returns role=article with focusable/describedby/keyshortcuts/roledescription and NO `expanded` property at all: `aria-expanded` is not supported on role=article, so even a correct value would never reach a screen reader.
findings.fix: Delete the dead state rather than resurrect it. In src/tasks.js: remove `openNoteId` (line 52) and every assignment; make line 428 `draggable="true"` unconditional; delete the `aria-expanded` term on line 430 entirely (role=article does not support it — the panel is a separate object and announces itself through the live region already); delete the `data-open` term on line 434 and the Escape branch at 2828-2832. In src/tasks.css delete lines 954, 956-957, 1179 and 1976. If the five-line note clamp still needs a way out, hang it off the panel that actually opens (`.taskPanel`), not off a card attribute nothing sets.

findings.element: .b-layout [data-layout-to] / [data-app="timeline"][data-layout] — src/timeline.js:176-178 `PHONE_T.addEventListener("change", function () { if (C.rootEl()... ) go("owner-flight"); })`, in the core IIFE that opens at src/timeline.js:26; `C` is only declared at src/timeline.js:331, inside the renderer's separate closure
findings.problem: `C` is not in scope at line 177, so every crossing of 720px throws `ReferenceError: C is not defined` (measured: Chromium pageerror at MediaQueryList.<anonymous>, on 768→721→700 and again on 700→900) and the re-mount never runs. The file's own header comment at src/timeline.js:4-8 states the contract this handler exists to keep — "the across composition is withheld on it, and crossing it re-mounts the owner's surface so the bar is never stale" — and it is not kept. Driven: load timeline.owner-flight at 1024 (data-layout="across", the Across/Down group present), resize to 700 → data-layout stays "across" and the Across/Down buttons are still on screen at phone width, against the locked decision "Across is never offered on a phone". `acrossAllowed()` (src/timeline.js:620) reads `!PHONE_T.matches` correctly, but only at render time, and nothing re-renders. The reverse is as bad: load at 700 (down, no toggle), widen to 1024 → still down, toggle still absent, so a desk user who narrowed the window once can never get the across composition back. The gates cannot see any of this because both open a fresh page per viewport and never cross the boundary.
findings.fix: Replace the body of the handler at src/timeline.js:177 with a plain re-mount in the scope it actually lives in — `mount();` — and nothing else. Do NOT call `go()`: `go()` (src/timeline.js:2318-2326) moves focus to `.b-pressTitle`/`.b-who`, and stealing focus to a heading because somebody dragged a window edge is a worse defect than the one being fixed. Add the same one-line remount to the tasks/notes pattern already in use (`PHONE.addEventListener("change", () => mount())`, src/tasks.js:4203) so all three products cross 720 the same way, and add one assertion to interaction-check.mjs that resizes an open page across 720 in both directions and requires zero pageerrors plus `[data-layout-to]` absent below 721.

findings.element: [data-app="tasks"][data-density="compact"] .when — src/tasks.css:2167 `[data-app="tasks"][data-density="compact"] .when { height: 18px; font-size: 10.5px; ... }`; the state is switched at src/tasks.js:3204-3208 from the Show menu's Display row (src/tasks.js:800)
findings.problem: Compact is a real, one-click state — Show → Compact, `root.setAttribute("data-density", "compact")` — and sixteen CSS rules key off it, but it is not in elevate.config.json's `states` list, so neither gate ever visits it. Driven (open Show, click Compact, at 1440 and at 1280): `.when` computes to font-size 10.5px, which is off the declared typeRamp in elevate.config.json (steps 10 and 11 exist; 10.5 does not). The same 10.5px is inherited by the `.sr` span inside it. In comfortable the same element is 11px, on the ladder. So the surface has a reachable configuration that would turn the `ramp` category of the currently-green measured gate red, and a half-pixel type size that buys 0.5px per glyph on the one piece of card metadata an operator reads on every row. The `sizeLadder`/`spaceLadder` exemption recorded in notes.ladders does not cover this: `typeRamp` IS declared in this config and IS gated.
findings.fix: Two edits. (1) src/tasks.css:2167 — set `font-size: 10px` (the ramp step below) or keep 11px and take the row height out of the type instead; nothing else in the suite is set at a half pixel. (2) elevate.config.json — add `tasks.compact` to `states` (the state handler already accepts it, and add the density to the state setter if it does not) so the density the operator can actually pick is inside the five-viewport audit rather than beside it. Then re-run gate.mjs and fix whatever else compact turns up.
